12433-narrative-of-the-voyage-of-h-m-s-r.creator: Unknown
12433-narrative-of-the-voyage-of-h-m-s-r.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. have contributed Appendices to this work--George Busk, Esquire F.R.S., Dr. Latham, Professor Edward Forbes, F.R.S., and Adam White, Esquire, F.L.S.--I have also to offer my best thanks. It also affords me great pleasure to record my obligations to T. Huxley, Esquire R.N., F.R.S.

arxiv-1709-01565.title: Energy dependent forward B → \rightarrow J / ψ J/\psi measurements in p+p collisions at PHENIX
arxiv-1709-01565.description: Abstract The heavy flavor studies at RHIC help improve the knowledge of the bottom/charm quark production and can test Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). Compared to the LHC/Tevatron, the RHIC heavy flavor production originates from different partonic sub-processes and has a complementary kinematic coverage.

arxiv-2011-11288.title: AutoGraph: Automated Graph Neural Network
arxiv-2011-11288.creator: Yaoman Li✉, Irwin King
arxiv-2011-11288.description: Abstract Graphs play an important role in many applications. Recently, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved promising results in graph analysis tasks. Some state-of-the-art GNN models have been proposed, e.g., Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), Graph Attention Networks (GATs), etc. Despite these successes, most of the GNNs only have shallow structure. This causes the low expressive power of the GNNs.

arxiv-2107-06406.title: A Theoretical Framework for Learning from Quantum Data
arxiv-2107-06406.creator: Mohsen Heidari, Arun Padakandla, Wojciech Szpankowski
arxiv-2107-06406.description: Abstract Over decades traditional information theory of source and channel coding advances toward learning and effective extraction of information from data. We propose to go one step further and offer a theoretical foundation for learning classical patterns from quantum data . However, there are several roadblocks to lay the groundwork for such a generalization.

arxiv-2206-05935.title: Fluorescence angiography classification in colorectal surgery
arxiv-2206-05935.creator: Antonio S Soares, Sophia Bano, Neil T Clancy, Laurence B Lovat, Danail Stoyanov, Manish Chand
arxiv-2206-05935.description: Abstract Background: Fluorescence angiography has shown very promising results in reducing anastomotic leaks by allowing the surgeon to select optimally perfused tissue. However, subjective interpretation of the fluorescent signal still hinders broad application of the technique, as significant variation between different surgeons exists.

arxiv-2404-15574.title: Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality
arxiv-2404-15574.creator: Wenhao Wu λ {\textlambda}, Yizhong Wang δ {\textdelta}, Guangxuan Xiao σ {\textsigma}, Hao Peng π {\textpi}, Yao Fu µ {\textmu}
arxiv-2404-15574.description: Abstract Despite the recent progress in long-context large language models (LLMs), it remains elusive how these transformer-based language models acquire the capability to retrieve relevant information from arbitrary locations within the long context. This paper aims to address this question.

arxiv-2409-16071.title: Learning with Confidence: Training Better Classifiers from Soft Labels
arxiv-2409-16071.creator: Sjoerd de Vries, Dirk Thierens
arxiv-2409-16071.description: Abstract In supervised machine learning, models are typically trained using data with hard labels, i.e., definite assignments of class membership. This traditional approach, however, does not take the inherent uncertainty in these labels into account. We investigate whether incorporating label uncertainty, represented as discrete probability distributions over the class labels—known as soft labels—improves the predictive performance of classification models.

arxiv-2411-10395.title: Optimising stochastic algorithms for hadron correlation function computations in lattice QCD using a localised distillation basis
arxiv-2411-10395.creator: Nicolas Lang, Robert G. Edwards, Michael J. Peardon, for the Hadron Spectrum Collaboration
arxiv-2411-10395.description: Abstract Distillation is a quark-smearing method for the construction of a broad class of hadron operators useful in lattice QCD computations and defined via a projection operator into a vector space of smooth gauge-covariant fields. A new orthonormal basis for this space is constructed which builds in locality.

arxiv-2412-14518.title: Efficient Self-Supervised Video Hashing with Selective State Spaces
arxiv-2412-14518.creator: Jinpeng Wang, Niu Lian, Jun Li, Yuting Wang, Yan Feng, Bin Chen, Yongbing Zhang, Shu-Tao Xia
arxiv-2412-14518.description: Abstract Self-supervised video hashing (SSVH) is a practical task in video indexing and retrieval. Although Transformers are predominant in SSVH for their impressive temporal modeling capabilities, they often suffer from computational and memory inefficiencies. Drawing inspiration from Mamba, an advanced state-space model, we explore its potential in SSVH to achieve a better balance between efficacy and efficiency.

arxiv-2504-08120.title: DeepSeek-R1 vs. o3-mini: How Well can Reasoning LLMs Evaluate MT and Summarization?
arxiv-2504-08120.creator: Daniil Larionov †, Sotaro Takeshita †, Ran Zhang †, Yanran Chen ⋄
arxiv-2504-08120.description: Abstract Reasoning-enabled large language models (LLMs) excel in logical tasks, yet their utility for evaluating natural language generation remains unexplored. This study systematically compares reasoning LLMs with non-reasoning counterparts across machine translation and text summarization evaluation tasks. We evaluate eight models spanning state-of-the-art reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI o3), their distilled variants (8B-70B parameters), and equivalent non-reasoning LLMs.

arxiv-2505-13688.title: Gaze-Enhanced Multimodal Turn-Taking Prediction in Triadic Conversations
arxiv-2505-13688.creator: Seongsil, Calvin, Michael, Christi
arxiv-2505-13688.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Seongsil, Calvin, Michael, Christi. Turn-taking prediction is crucial for seamless interactions. This study introduces a novel, lightweight framework for accurate turn-taking prediction in triadic conversations without relying on computationally intensive methods. Unlike prior approaches that either disregard gaze or treat it as a passive signal, our model integrates gaze with speaker localization, structuring it within a spatial constraint to transform it into a reliable predictive cue.

arxiv-2601-16172.title: Structured Hints for Sample-Efficient Lean Theorem Proving
arxiv-2601-16172.creator: Zac Burton
arxiv-2601-16172.description: Abstract State-of-the-art neural theorem provers like DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 combine large language models with reinforcement learning, achieving impressive results through sophisticated training. We ask: do these highly-trained models still benefit from simple structural guidance at inference time? We evaluate a lightweight intervention—a fixed prompt schedule over 15 common tactic skeletons—on the miniF2F benchmark. This simple approach yields 21.7% pass@16 compared to 15.

pmc-10544441.title: Hyperlipidemia in immune thrombocytopenia: a retrospective study
pmc-10544441.creator: Shouqing Han, Hui Lu, Yafei Yu, Xinguang Liu, Fangmiao Jing, Liang Wang, Yajing Zhao, Ming Hou
pmc-10544441.description: BackgroundImmune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune hemorrhagic disease characterized by low platelet count and bleeding manifestations. However, some patients also suffered from atherosclerosis or even infarction. Apart from activated platelets, lipid metabolism takes a large part in the formation of atherosclerosis and metabolic syndrome. The lipid metabolic state in ITP patients is still unknown.

pmc-10613264.title: Cohabitation with aggressive hosts: description of a new microhisterid species in nests of a ponerine ant with ecological notes
pmc-10613264.creator: Gabriela Pérez-Lachaud, Nicolas Degallier, Yves Gomy, Manuel Elías-Gutiérrez, Franklin H Rocha, Jean-Paul Lachaud
pmc-10613264.description: A new clown beetle species, Bacanius neoponerae, is described from Mexican nests of the arboreal ponerine ant Neoponera villosa found in the tank bromeliad Aechmea bracteata. Adult beetles were found in brood chambers or inner refuse piles, but also outside the ant nests, in decaying organic matter between the bromeliad leaves.

pmc-10638317.title: The impact of the land-to-sea transition on evolutionary integration and modularity of the pinniped backbone
pmc-10638317.creator: Juan Miguel Esteban, Alberto Martín-Serra, Alejandro Pérez-Ramos, Baptiste Mulot, Katrina Jones, Borja Figueirido
pmc-10638317.description: In this study, we investigate how the terrestrial-aquatic transition influenced patterns of axial integration and modularity in response to the secondary adaptation to a marine lifestyle. We use 3D geometric morphometrics to quantify shape covariation among presacral vertebrae in pinnipeds (Carnivora; Pinnipedia) and to compare with patterns of axial integration and modularity in their close terrestrial relatives.

pmc-11331716.title: Unusual radiologic imaging in juvenile granulosa cell tumor with precocious puberty: A unilocular cyst
pmc-11331716.creator: Nurmilia Afriliani, Tri Wulanhandarini
pmc-11331716.description: Juvenile Granulosa Cell Tumor (JGCT) represents 5% of all granulosa cell cancers. Precocious puberty is a frequent feature of this tumor. A 2-year and 2-month-old girl was referred with a diagnosis of suspected ovarian cancer, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, and precocious puberty. Radiologic examination revealed the following: Abdominal ultrasonography showed a solitary anechoic cystic lesion in the pelvic cavity.

pmc-11358616.title: Distribution of bat species in Western Asia: Occurrence records from the Western Asia Bat Research Network (WAB-Net) project
pmc-11358616.creator: Kendra Phelps, Zahran Al Abdulasalam, Nisreen Al-Hmoud, Shahzad Ali, Mumen Alrwashdeh, Attaullah, Rasit Bilgin, Astghik Ghazaryan, Luke Hamel, Nijat Hasanov, Ioseb Natradze, George Papov, Ketevan Sidamonidze, Andrew Spalton, Lela Urushadze, Kevin J Olival
pmc-11358616.description: BackgroundWestern Asia represents a mixing pot of diverse bat species with distributions spanning across other geographic regions. Yet, relative to other regions, there is a significant gap in coordinated bat research in Western Asia, thereby resulting in a relatively limited number of curated occurrence records.

pmc-11493094.title: Learning from employer experiences with paid leave policy expansions during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11493094.creator: William H Dow, Julia M Goodman, Paloma Lin, Paige Park
pmc-11493094.description: The United States does not have a federal policy offering employees paid leave. We study employer attitudes toward the Families First Coronavirus Response Act (FFCRA) federal emergency paid leave policies temporarily adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic to draw lessons for proposed permanent federal paid leave policies.

pmc-11507131.title: Deciphering Immunotoxicity in Animal-Derived Biomaterials: A Genomic and Bioinformatics Approach
pmc-11507131.creator: Huan Lian, Yu Liu, Linnan Ke, Qianqian Han, Patrick M Dansette
pmc-11507131.description: Immunotoxicity evaluation has been crucial in preclinical testing for implantable animal-derived biomaterials due to their prolonged contact with the human body, which requires stringent safety assessments. By creating experimental models with varying levels of immunotoxicity, this study reveals the decisive role of decellularization treatment in diminishing the immunogenicity of materials, thus ensuring clinical safety.

pmc-11519536.title: Deep learning based local feature classification to automatically identify single molecule fluorescence events
pmc-11519536.creator: Shuqi Zhou, Yu Miao, Haoren Qiu, Yuan Yao, Wenjuan Wang, Chunlai Chen
pmc-11519536.description: Long-term single-molecule fluorescence measurements are widely used powerful tools to study the conformational dynamics of biomolecules in real time to further elucidate their conformational dynamics. Typically, thousands or even more single-molecule traces are analyzed to provide statistically meaningful information, which is labor-intensive and can introduce user bias. Recently, several deep-learning models have been developed to automatically classify single-molecule traces.

pmc-11546613.title: Permeability and Toxicity of Cryoprotective Agents in Silkworm Embryos: Impact on Cryopreservation
pmc-11546613.creator: David Urbán-Duarte, Shuichiro Tomita, Hiroki Sakai, Hideki Sezutsu, Horacio Álvarez-Gallardo, Yooichi Kainoh, Seiichi Furukawa, Keiro Uchino, Hiroko Tabunoki, Satomi Adegawa
pmc-11546613.description: The permeation of cryoprotectants into insect embryos is critical for successful cryopreservation. However, the permeability of silkworm embryos to cryoprotectants and the effects of cryopreservation remain poorly studied. In this study, we evaluated the permeability and toxicity of four cryoprotective agents (CPAs) as well as the vitrification effect on the viability of silkworm embryos.

pmc-12808431.title: The neoadjuvant esophageal score: a prognostic tool for predicting survival and postoperative complications in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-12808431.creator: Hao Chen, Xuan Huang, Cheng Huang, Qichang Xie, Chun Chen, Bin Zheng, Yuxing Lin, Renjie Huang, Li Cheng, Zhang Yang, Chi Xu
pmc-12808431.description: BackgroundEsophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains a major global health challenge, and reliable prognostic markers. We developed and validated the Neoadjuvant Esophageal (NAE) score, derived from treatment response, to predict overall survival (OS) and postoperative complications in locally advanced ESCC.

pmc-12985884.title: Relapsing Pericarditis: Prediction of Relapses, Risk Scores, and Role of Exercise Restriction
pmc-12985884.creator: Joseph El Roumi, Jibran Ikram, Tom Kai Ming Wang
pmc-12985884.description: Relapsing pericarditis (RP) is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by two or more episodes of acute pericarditis flares after a minimum of a 4-week symptom-free period. Recurrent pericarditis develops in approximately 15% to 30% of patients following an initial episode of acute pericarditis, and nearly half of these individuals experience subsequent recurrences.

pmc-13216642.title: The formation and function of intercellular bridges in male germlines
pmc-13216642.creator: Jian Cui, Jiaxuan Cheng, Bingbing Wu, Andong He
pmc-13216642.description: Intercellular bridges (ICBs) are fundamental and evolutionarily conserved structures in spermatogenesis, with roles that extend far beyond simple cytoplasmic connections. These stable conduits, which connect synchronously developing germ cells, are crucial for cytoplasmic sharing and intercellular communication. This review highlights the core regulatory machinery governing ICBs dynamics, including their formation and function, in mouse and Drosophila melanogaster.

pmc-13381418.title: Phytochemical characterization and bioactivity evaluation of Artemisia abyssinica methanolic extract as a baseline for bioresource exploration
pmc-13381418.creator: Abdu Aldarhami, Suliman A. Alderhami, Hassen Harzali, Abdulrahman S. Bazaid, Zarah I. Alzahrani, Hassan A. El-Adawy, Nashwa H. Abdullah, Nizar H. Saeedi, Khaled A. Abdelshafeek, Ahmed A. Elhenawy
pmc-13381418.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The growing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and cancer has intensified interest in natural products as sources of biologically active compounds with potential pharmaceutical relevance. In this study, the phytochemical composition of the methanolic extract of Artemisia abyssinica aerial parts (MEAA) was comprehensively characterized using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and its in vitro antimicrobial, antioxidant, cytotoxic, and molecular docking properties were evaluated.

pmc-13384707.title: A hidden tunnel at the skull base: A descriptive anatomical study of the mastoid foramen in dry skulls
pmc-13384707.creator: Ceren Uğuz Gençer, Mustafa Deniz Yörük, Zeynep Nisa Karakoyun, Hasan Tetiker, Mehmet İlkay Koşar
pmc-13384707.description: The mastoid foramen (MF) is a small but clinically significant anatomical structure located on the mastoid process of the temporal bone, showing considerable individual variation in its morphology and localization. This descriptive morphometric study aimed to provide data relevant to surgical planning by defining the frequency, morphometric characteristics, and relationship of the mastoid foramen with bony reference points.

pmc-13429682.title: NMR-based metabolomics analysis in breast cancer patients from Saudi Arabia: a pilot study
pmc-13429682.creator: Muhammad Ikram Ullah, Shazia Rashid, Aisha Tahir, Ayman Ali Mohammed Alameen, Aisha Farhana, Tarig Mohamed Fadl Elmula, Ziad H. Al-Oanzi
pmc-13429682.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In breast cancer (BC), metabolomic profiles have largely focused on Western and East Asian groups, with limited data from the Middle East. Population-specific studies are required to better understand metabolite alterations due to regional, environmental and genetic heterogeneity. This exploratory pilot study aimed to evaluate serum metabolic alterations in breast cancer patients and their associations with disease stage using NMR-based metabolomics in the Saudi Arabian cohort. A total of 30 female breast cancer patients and 30 healthy controls were included.

pmc-13526734.title: Clinicopathological discordance and survival outcomes in 154 breast cancer patients with pulmonary metastasis in a real-world setting
pmc-13526734.creator: Ying Yan, Yifei Chen, Lijun Di, Xu Liang, Bin Shao, Hanfang Jiang, Guohong Song, Huiping Li

pmc-13559039.title: Right Heart Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Profiles and Cardiopulmonary Reserve in Older Adults Undergoing Long‐Term Multicomponent Exercise: A 2‐Year Longitudinal Study
pmc-13559039.creator: Tingting Liu, Yanmei Song, Zhiqiang Ye, Cai Jiang, Yanling Cheng, Yalan Dai, Huijuan Zhong, Feng Huang, Qiaowei Li, Fang Wang
pmc-13559039.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Right heart geometry and function are essential for preserving physical performance in healthy aging, yet evidence regarding how long‐term supervised multicomponent exercise influences right heart characteristics and cardiopulmonary reserve over time remains limited. To address this gap, this interim analysis of a prospective, non‐randomized, two‐armed cohort study included 155 adults aged ≥ 65 years assigned to supervised multicomponent training (n = 75) or education control group (n = 80).

pmc-13560026.title: Single-cell mapping of homocysteine-induced perturbations in avian embryogenesis using LMO and BD rhapsody transcriptomics
pmc-13560026.creator: Stéphanie Maupetit-Méhouas, Felipe Maurelia, Pouria Hosseinnia, Nicolas Allègre, Yoan Renaud, Jonas Cruzel, Claire Chazaud, Charlène Guillot
pmc-13560026.description: SummarySingle-cell RNA sequencing enables the study of cellular heterogeneity and the effects of environmental perturbations across complex tissues. However, subtle biological responses can be obscured by experimental noise, sample-specific processing, and computational integration. Here, we combined lipid-modified oligonucleotide cell tagging with the BD Rhapsody platform to multiplex early embryonic chick cells exposed to different homocysteine conditions.

pmc-13666559.title: Role of immune cell subsets in liver fibrosis through single-cell RNA sequencing and array
pmc-13666559.creator: Bo Yang, Junjie Yuan, Jingwen Zhao, Xin Chen
pmc-13666559.description: BackgroundImmune-inflammatory responses and dysregulation play a key role in liver fibrosis (LF) and cirrhosis progression, but the phenotypic and functional dynamics of immune cell populations remain poorly characterized.MethodsLF-related data from the GEO database were analyzed using ssGSEA to quantify immune cell infiltration and Kaplan-Meier analysis to assess the prognostic value of specific immune cell populations.
